name: Dennis
heroAlt: Dennis seated in a tropical garden in warm golden evening light
tributeHtml:
He gave us music, laughter
and a welcome that felt like home.
shareDescription: A personal memorial song created from his story.
lyrics:
Dennis had the radio playing
Before the kettle went on
A little bassline in the morning
While he hummed and sang along

Shirt pressed clean for Sundays
Shoes polished by the door
And when he stepped into the kitchen
The whole house smiled once more

He had a way of making trouble
Feel smaller than before
With one old joke, one knowing look
One laugh across the floor

Dennis, you gave us the music
You gave us the laughter too
You gave us stories round the table
And the songs that carried you
Dennis, your love keeps on giving
In the little things we do
And when we hear those old tunes playing
We feel closer to you

Dominoes slapped on the table
He would lean in with his cheeky grin
Saying, “Watch and learn now, children”
Like he knew he had the win
Sunday pot was gently rolling
Old tunes floating through the air
And every cousin, child and neighbour
Knew there’d be a welcome there

He was father, he was uncle
He was brother, he was friend
And the rhythm that he gave us
Still comes round again

Dennis, you gave us the music
You gave us the laughter too
You gave us stories round the table
And the songs that carried you
Dennis, your love keeps on giving
In the little things we do
And when we hear those old tunes playing
We feel closer to you

So play it low and sweet now
Let the bassline roll with grace
Tell the stories how he told them
Let the tears fall where they may
He would say, “Hold up your head now”
He would say, “Don’t lose your way”
And somehow we can hear him
In the songs we play today

Dennis, you gave us the music
You gave us the laughter too
You gave us stories round the table
And the songs that carried you
Dennis, your love keeps on giving
In the little things we do
And when we hear those old tunes playing
We feel closer to you
rememberingParagraphs: Dennis filled ordinary days with music, humour and warmth. Whether the radio was playing, dominoes were on the table or Sunday food was gently cooking, there was always laughter nearby and room for one more person.

He shared his life with his wife, June, and was a proud father to Andrea and Simon. Family sat at the centre of everything, and the home they made together became a place where relatives, friends and neighbours were always welcomed.

After years working as a bus driver, Dennis was remembered by passengers and colleagues for his easy conversation, steady nature and familiar smile. Those old tunes still bring him close, and the rhythm he gave his family continues in the stories they tell and the love they carry forward.
closingLine: Forever loved. Always close in the music.
storyParagraphs: Dennis was born in 1951 and grew up in a home where music was never far away. The radio was often playing before the day had properly begun, and he developed a lifelong love for basslines, old records and the kind of songs that could bring a room together.

He later met June, whose warmth and good sense balanced his humour and mischief perfectly. Together they built a lively family home and raised their daughter, Andrea, and their son, Simon. Dennis was proud of them both and followed every stage of their lives with interest, advice and plenty of teasing.

For many years Dennis worked as a bus driver. He liked the rhythm of the route, the familiar faces and the brief conversations that became part of each working day. Regular passengers came to recognise his voice and his smile, while colleagues knew him as someone who could keep calm, make people laugh and help a difficult shift feel easier.

At home, Sundays had their own rhythm. June would be preparing food while Dennis kept the music playing and offered commentary from nearby. Andrea, Simon, relatives, friends and neighbours came and went, and somehow there was always enough to go around. Dennis made people feel welcome without ceremony; there was simply a place for them.

Dominoes were part of family gatherings and evenings with friends. Dennis played with confidence, a cheeky grin and plenty of talk, especially when he thought he had the winning hand. The game was never only about winning. It was about stories, laughter, friendly rivalry and the pleasure of everyone being together.

Dennis showed his love in everyday ways: through music, food, lifts home, encouragement and presence. He reminded Andrea and Simon to hold their heads up and not lose their way. The warmth he created with June still lives in the songs the family plays, the meals they share and the stories that bring his laughter back into the room.
